ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a mass spectrum, with the vertical axis labeled relative abundance (%) and the horizontal axis labeled atomic mass. The peaks are labeled Zr-90, Zr-91, Zr-92, Zr-94, and Zr-96, among which the highest peak is Zr-90. Reasoning: The most common isotope corresponds to the peak with the highest relative abundance in the mass spectrum, so the most common isotope of zirconium is Zr-90. The atomic number of zirconium is 40, therefore it has 40 protons. Number of neutrons = mass number − number of protons = 90 − 40 = 50.
